svg.title: A 100 MiB file at default settings
svg.desc: A 100 MiB file becomes 101 encrypted data chunks in four stripes of 32, 32, 32 and 5 data chunks with 16, 16, 16 and 3 outer parity chunks. One chunk is shown as a group of 32 fragment slots: 16 data fragments, 8 guaranteed parity fragments and 8 extra parity fragments. Three manifest copies are separate groups.
svg.text: A 100 MiB file at default settings
104,857,600 bytes become 101 data chunks, 4 stripes, 155 groups and 3,720 guaranteed fragments
Each 1,048,560-byte piece (chunkSize − 16) is sealed with AES-256-GCM into a 1 MiB chunk; the last holds 1,600 bytes plus padding.
any 5 of these 8 groups rebuild the stripe
Chunk 2 of stripe 3, sequence 98, as a group: inner code RS(16, 16), 32 slots of 65,536 bytes
16 data fragments: 64 KiB slices of the chunk
Any 16 of the 32 slots rebuild the chunk. The 24 guaranteed fragments go to 24 different gridnodes, the extras to spare ranks.
each copy is its own group: replicated, not outer coded
